title: Relier une idée sans perdre la préposition
summary: Choose relative pronouns for subjects, objects, places, things and people, retaining the verb's required preposition.
objectives: Distinguish tout ce qui from tout ce que by clause function.
Choose où or dans lequel for a place, not mechanically for time.
Use preposition + qui/lequel and correctly contract à + lequel forms.

sources.label: Académie française: relative quoi and its antecedents

sections.title: Everything that: identify the missing role
paragraphs: A relative clause describes or identifies a referent. An antecedent is the noun or expression it points back to. In tout ce qui/que, there is no specific noun antecedent: tout ce means everything/all that. Tout ce qui supplies the subject of the following verb; tout ce que supplies its direct object.

Find the missing function rather than looking only at the next word. In tout ce qui me plaît, qui is the subject even though me appears before plaît. In tout ce que tu proposes, tu is the subject and que is what you propose. Que elides to qu' before a vowel. Tout ce is neutral singular and uses singular agreement when it is a subject.

examples.french: **Tout ce qui** manque est indiqué en rouge.
examples.english: Everything that is missing is marked in red.
examples.note: Qui is the subject of manque.

examples.french: Je noterai **tout ce que** vous proposerez.
examples.english: I will write down everything you propose.
examples.note: Vous is subject; que is object.

examples.french: **Tout ce qui** me semble utile sera conservé.
examples.english: Everything that seems useful to me will be kept.
examples.note: Me does not turn qui into an object.

mistakes.avoid: Tout ce que manque est ici.
mistakes.prefer: Tout ce qui manque est ici.
mistakes.why: The relative expression supplies the subject of manque.

sections.title: Où is broader than dans lequel
paragraphs: Où can refer to a place or a time. For a place meaning 'in which', dans lequel/laquelle/lesquels/lesquelles can make the relationship explicit. Lequel forms agree with the antecedent: masculine singular lequel, feminine singular laquelle, masculine/mixed plural lesquels, feminine plural lesquelles.

Do not replace a time-relative où mechanically with dans lequel: le jour où nous sommes partis is the normal construction. For places, choose the actual relationship too: the bridge on which you stand requires sur lequel, not dans lequel.

examples.english: The workshop where we work is bright.

examples.french: L'atelier **dans lequel** nous travaillons est lumineux.
examples.english: The workshop in which we work is bright.
examples.note: An explicit in-which alternative; un atelier is masculine.

examples.french: Les salles **dans lesquelles** nous répétons sont petites.
examples.english: The rooms in which we rehearse are small.
examples.note: Une salle is feminine; plural agreement.

examples.french: Le jour **où** nous avons signé, il neigeait.
examples.english: On the day we signed, it was snowing.
examples.note: Time où does not license a mechanical dans lequel replacement.

mistakes.avoid: La salle dans lequel nous attendons est vide.
mistakes.prefer: La salle dans laquelle nous attendons est vide.
mistakes.why: Laquelle agrees with feminine singular salle.

sections.title: Choose the relationship before choosing the pronoun
paragraphs: After a preposition such as avec, pour, sans, sur or derrière, lequel and its agreeing forms are the normal choice for a named thing antecedent. For people, qui is usually natural; lequel forms are also possible, particularly to clarify the antecedent. Do not use qui after a preposition for a thing merely because English uses which/that similarly. Neutral antecedents such as ce have a different pattern, explained below.

The preposition belongs to the verb or relation: compter sur (rely on), travailler avec (work with), voter pour (vote for). Keep it in the relative clause. À + lequel contracts to auquel; à + lesquels/lesquelles gives auxquels/auxquelles; à laquelle stays two words. With people, à qui is also available. Participer à, répondre à and s'intéresser à do not become direct-object verbs in a relative clause.
points: The full à series is auquel, à laquelle, auxquels, auxquelles.
No contraction with other prepositions here: avec lequel, pour laquelle, sur lesquels, derrière lesquelles.

examples.french: La collègue **avec qui** je travaille connaît le quartier.
examples.english: The colleague I work with knows the area.
examples.note: A person: avec laquelle would also be grammatical.

examples.french: Le mur **derrière lequel** le jardin se trouve est ancien.
examples.english: The wall behind which the garden lies is old.
examples.note: An agreeing lequel form is the normal choice for this named thing.

examples.french: Les outils **sur lesquels** nous comptons sont fiables.
examples.english: The tools we rely on are reliable.

examples.french: La question **à laquelle** je réponds est précise.
examples.english: The question I am answering is precise.

examples.french: Le groupe **auquel** j'appartiens se réunit ici.
examples.english: The group I belong to meets here.
examples.note: Appartenir à plus masculine singular contracts.

examples.french: Les personnes **à qui** j'ai parlé attendent dehors.
examples.english: The people I spoke to are waiting outside.
examples.note: Auxquelles is also legitimate; à qui is natural for people.

sections.title: Ce à quoi, quelque chose sur quoi
paragraphs: Not every antecedent names a masculine or feminine thing. Ce, rien and quelque chose can stand for an unspecified idea or thing. After a preposition, quoi is natural with these neutral antecedents: ce à quoi, rien contre quoi, quelque chose sur quoi. Neutral means that the expression does not supply an ordinary noun gender for agreement; it does not mean that the idea is unimportant.

Keep the required preposition just as with lequel: s'attendre à gives ce à quoi on s'attend. Quoi can also refer back to an entire statement or event, especially in a linking phrase such as après quoi. With an ordinary named noun, an agreeing lequel form is usually clearer and more common. Literary or formal nominal uses of quoi exist too, so 'quoi can never be relative' is not a valid rule.
points: For a simple de-complement, ce dont is often lighter than ce de quoi; the next lesson explains dont.

examples.french: C'est **ce à quoi** nous réfléchissons depuis lundi.
examples.english: That is what we have been thinking about since Monday.
examples.note: Réfléchir à supplies à; ce is a neutral antecedent.
The thing is unspecified; sur expresses the surface relationship.

examples.french: Le traitement est terminé, **après quoi** les pièces doivent refroidir.
examples.english: The treatment is finished, after which the parts must cool.
examples.note: Quoi refers to the preceding stage as a whole.

examples.french: La proposition **à laquelle** nous réfléchissons vient du comité.
examples.english: The proposal we are thinking about comes from the committee.
examples.note: A named feminine noun uses the normal agreeing form, unlike ce à quoi.

mistakes.why: Neutral ce does not provide a masculine noun antecedent for auquel.

practice.prompt: Supply the relative after à: Ce à ___ je m'oppose, c'est la fermeture de la bibliothèque.
practice.explanation: Neutral ce + preposition takes quoi; s'opposer supplies à.

practice.prompt: What does quoi refer to in Elle a fourni les justificatifs, après quoi le paiement a été autorisé?
choices: The preceding event of supplying the documents.
answers: The preceding event of supplying the documents.
practice.explanation: Après quoi can point back to an entire preceding event, not just one gendered noun.

practice.prompt: Use the neutral relative quoi with sur. Supply both words: Il nous faut quelque chose ___ poser ce vase.
practice.explanation: Quelque chose can be followed by a preposition plus quoi, here before an infinitive.

practice.prompt: Now the antecedent is a named feminine noun. Use the agreeing lequel form after sans: La méthode sans ___ le calcul serait impossible est expliquée ici.
practice.explanation: The explicit instruction asks for feminine singular laquelle, referring to méthode.

practice.prompt: Complete using à + quoi, preserving s'attendre à: Ce ___ nous nous attendions ne s'est pas produit.
practice.explanation: The preposition belongs to s'attendre; neutral ce has no gender for lequel agreement.

practice.prompt: Link the next action to the whole preceding event using après + quoi: Nous installerons les capteurs, ___ nous lancerons les mesures.
practice.explanation: Quoi refers to installing the sensors as an event.

practice.prompt: Supply qui or que: Je garde tout ce ___ peut servir.
practice.explanation: The relative is the subject of peut.

practice.prompt: Replace où by an explicit 'in which' phrase: La maison où elle habite. Supply only the replacement.
practice.explanation: Maison is feminine singular.

practice.prompt: Supply the relative after avec for a feminine person: La bénévole avec ___ je travaille.
practice.explanation: Both qui and feminine laquelle are legitimate for a person.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete à-relative: Le projet ___ nous participons avance.
practice.explanation: Participer à + masculine singular lequel contracts.

practice.prompt: Supply qui or que: Tout ce ___ nous avons préparé est prêt.
practice.explanation: Nous is subject; que is the direct object of préparer.

practice.prompt: Supply qui or que: Tout ce ___ vous inquiète mérite une réponse.
practice.explanation: Vous is object here; qui is the subject that causes worry.

practice.prompt: Supply the explicit 'in which' phrase: Les bureaux ___ nous travaillons sont fermés.
practice.explanation: Bureaux is masculine plural.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete sur-relative: La table ___ le dossier est posé est ronde.
practice.explanation: The dossier is on, not inside, the table.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete à-relative: Les demandes ___ nous répondons sont urgentes.
practice.explanation: À + feminine plural lesquelles contracts.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete à-relative: Les clubs ___ il appartient recrutent.
practice.explanation: À + masculine plural lesquels contracts.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete à-relative referring to a woman: La chercheuse ___ tu écris est en congé.
practice.explanation: Both forms work for a person.

practice.prompt: Choose the ordinary time-relative construction.
choices: L'année dans laquelle nous avons déménagé.
practice.explanation: The benchmark's dans lequel alternative concerns spatial in-which relationships, not routine substitution for time où.

practice.prompt: Supply the elided relative: Voici tout ce ___ elle recommande.
practice.explanation: Que is the object and elides before elle.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete sans-relative: Le logiciel ___ nous ne pouvons pas travailler est en panne.
practice.explanation: Masculine singular thing after sans.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete à-relative: La formation ___ elle s'intéresse commence en mai.
practice.explanation: S'intéresser à keeps à; feminine singular does not contract.

practice.prompt: Supply the explicit 'in which' phrase: Les boîtes ___ les livres sont rangés sont lourdes.
practice.explanation: Boîtes is feminine plural.

production_task.prompt: Introduce a local project to a new volunteer. Mention everything that matters, a person you work with, a place you use and a project you participate in. Use four relative clauses.
production_task.model_answer: Tout ce qui concerne la sécurité est affiché ici. La personne avec qui je travaille vous accueillera. La salle dans laquelle nous préparons les repas est au fond. Le projet auquel nous participons aide les familles du quartier.
production_task.translation: Everything concerning safety is displayed here. The person I work with will welcome you. The room in which we prepare meals is at the back. The project we participate in helps families in the neighbourhood.
rubric: Qui and que reflect the missing grammatical role.
Each preposition matches the relationship or verb.
Lequel forms agree with their antecedents.
People may use qui without being incorrectly forced into lequel.
